```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")
beer <- aus_production |> filter(!is.na(Beer)) |> select(Quarter, Beer)

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab00", title = "TSA review")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "Seasonal naive (SNAIVE) sets the forecast equal to which past value?",
  q2 = "An additive decomposition writes the series as which sum?",
  q3 = "After the last SES update, multi-step forecasts are:",
  q4 = "In one or two sentences, what pattern do you see in Australian beer production?"
)
```

## What you will do

Read graphics, keep a naive baseline, and check one SES step by hand.

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `fpp3`, `learnr`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

## Graphics

```{r beer-plot, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
beer |> autoplot(Beer) + labs(title = "Australian beer", y = "megalitres")
beer |> gg_season(Beer)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("The last observation from the same season", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The sample mean"),
  answer("A linear drift from the first observation"),
  answer("The residual from STL"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Trend + seasonal + remainder", correct = TRUE),
  answer("AR + MA + drift"),
  answer("Level times season only"),
  answer("White noise"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## SES hand check

$y=(10,12,11)$, $\alpha=0.5$, $\ell_0=10$.

```{r ses-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
y <- c(10, 12, 11)
alpha <- 0.5
ell <- 10
for (t in seq_along(y)) ell <- alpha * y[t] + (1 - alpha) * ell
ell
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("Flat (all equal to the last level)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Linear in h"),
  answer("Seasonal"),
  answer("Zero"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Trend? season? stable or growing swings?",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Answer the questions above first, type your name, download the `.txt`, and upload it.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
